nodes.description: In mice, deleting alphaV from myeloid cells, or alphaVbeta8 from dendritic cells, reduces colonic regulatory T cells, increases activated T cells and causes severe colitis and autoimmunity. Gut macrophages and dendritic cells lacking alphaV also clear apoptotic cells poorly. Patients with ITGAV deficiency develop very early onset colitis refractory to medical therapy, and itgav knockout zebrafish develop colitis with raised inflammatory cytokine expression.

nodes.description: Biallelic ITGAV variants reduce or abolish functional integrin alphaV, either by aberrant splicing with nonsense-mediated decay or by a missense change that blocks trafficking of the alphaV heterodimer to the cell surface. Every alphaV integrin (alphaVbeta1, beta3, beta5, beta6, beta8) is affected because alphaV is their shared subunit. This is the initiating lesion.

nodes.description: TGF-beta is secreted bound to its latency-associated peptide and needs the RGD-binding integrins alphaVbeta6 and alphaVbeta8 to become active. In mice, abolishing the integrin-binding RGD motif of latent TGF-beta1 reproduces the vascular, inflammatory and immune features of TGF-beta1 deficiency even though latent TGF-beta1 is made normally. ITGAV deficiency removes both activating integrins at once.

nodes.description: Microglia need locally activated TGF-beta to mature. In mice, deleting the alphaVbeta8 integrin from the central nervous system arrests microglia in a dysmature state and causes a neurodevelopmental syndrome with oligodendrocyte maturation arrest, interneuron loss and spastic neuromotor dysfunction. itgav knockout zebrafish lose resident microglia, and the authors of the human report propose microglial dysfunction as a contributor to the brain disease of ITGAV deficiency.
